claims.text: In Table B.18.A of the December 2020 Stress Test Results, JPMorgan Chase & Co.'s common equity tier 1 capital ratio was 12.4 percent actual in 2020:Q2, with a projected ending ratio of 10.8 percent and projected minimum of 10.0 percent under the Federal Reserve's severely adverse scenario.

claims.text: The 12.4 percent figure is an actual regulatory ratio reported for 2020:Q2, whereas the 10.8 percent (ending) and 10.0 percent (minimum) figures are hypothetical Federal Reserve projections under the severely adverse scenario; the note states these are 'hypothetical estimates' and the minimum applies over 2020:Q3–2022:Q3.

citations.quotation:
These
projections represent hypothetical estimates that involve an economic outcome that is more adverse than expected. The minimum capital ratios are for the period 2020:Q3 to
2022:Q3.

counterarguments.text: The source text itself cautions that the projected figures are hypothetical estimates of a more-adverse-than-expected outcome, so the ending and minimum ratios should not be interpreted as forecasts of JPMorgan's actual capital position.

counterarguments.text: The minimum is a trough over the projection window (2020:Q3–2022:Q3), not a point-in-time value, so comparing it directly with the 2020:Q2 actual could be misleading.
